projects.name: Dev Log · User guide
projects.description: The Dev Log guide, written with the program itself: each note is a chapter with real examples and requests to copy and paste into the assistant. Start with note 1.0 and follow your route in Pending.

versions.instructions:
Start here
This guide is a Dev Log project: each note is a chapter, read top to bottom, from oldest to newest. What you see here is what you will do in your own projects.

How it is organized
1.1 · Projects
1.2 · Versions and notes
1.3 · Pending
2.0 · Save and backups
2.1 · Export
2.2 · Encryption and APIs copy
3.0 · Connect a model
3.1 · Quick actions and questions
3.2 · The assistant runs the program
3.3 · Analyze changes
3.4 · Rewrite and renumber versions
To jump to a topic, type a word in “Search versions…”.

Your route
The Pending list of this guide is your route: tick each step as you do it. To keep the guide intact, practice in a project of your own (chapter 1.1).

Requests to copy and paste
Lines in monospaced type are requests for the assistant. Copy them, paste them into the box of the AI panel (AI button, top right) and press Send. The ones under “without AI” headings run locally: they work with no model connected. Copy them exactly: with different wording they may stop running locally. The ones under “with AI” headings are answered by a model and need one connected (chapter 3.0).

Try it now · without AI
open help
show the pending tasks
search in the notes "underline"
The last one filters the history: only the notes with that word remain. To remove the filter, clear the text in “Search versions…”.

Projects
A project is a notebook: name, description, icon, version history, assistant conversation and pending tasks. Every project is independent.

Create one
Press + Project. Type a name (it suggests “My project”), a description if you want and, optionally, an icon with Upload icon. Create project opens it with a first, empty note: 1.0.

Edit, export and delete
In the project header: Edit changes name, description and icon; Export creates a TXT, DOCX or PDF of the project (chapter 2.1); Delete asks for confirmation and removes the project with its whole history. Right after, a notice with Undo appears and stays a few seconds. If it disappears, for 10 minutes you can still recover it with a request (at the end of this chapter).

Search and move around
The sidebar orders projects by last update: the one you modified last goes to the top. “Search project…” filters by name and also by the content of the notes. To remove the filter, clear the text.

Practice · without AI
Create your practice project; the other chapters use it.
create a project called Practice
To jump between projects by name:
select the project Dev Log
select the project Practice
To filter the list:
search in the projects "backup"
To recover the last thing you deleted even if the notice is gone (valid for 10 minutes; it undoes one action):
undo

Versions and notes
Each meaningful step is a version: a note with its number, its dates and what you did, why and what is left. They are listed from oldest to newest; CURRENT marks the last one and the rest are HISTORY.

Create and duplicate
New version note (at the top and at the end of the history) adds an empty note with the number after the last one: after 2.1 it suggests 2.2. Duplicate copies the text of a note into a new one at the end, with that same next number. Both are buttons: without AI there is no chat request to create or duplicate notes (with a model connected, the assistant can: chapter 3.2).
The number is edited in the field next to VERSION. It accepts 1, 1.0, 1.1 or v4.1: you decide what is a milestone (1.0, 2.0) and what is work inside it (1.1, 1.2).

Write and format
INSTRUCTIONS & NOTES is free text. The format bar changes the font (Sans, Serif or Mono), size (12 to 24), bold, italic, underline and strikethrough of the selection or, with no selection, of what you type next. Shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd+B, I and U; Ctrl/Cmd+Z also undoes formatting. The text stays plain text: search and the AI context do not change.

Actions on each note
At the top: Analyze changes (chapter 3.3), Duplicate and Delete, which asks for confirmation and leaves a notice with Undo. At the bottom: Copy text (puts “VERSION n” and the instructions on the clipboard), Export (chapter 2.1) and Select note, which marks it as active for the assistant. When there are notes out of view, the ▲ ▼ arrows appear and scroll the view by almost one screen.

Practice · without AI
In Practice, write the sentence “My first practice sentence” in note 1.0 and paste these requests. With no note number, they act on the selected note:
select the note 1.0
make it bold, size 16
With a number you do not need to select. A fragment goes in double quotes:
make it italic in note 1.0
make "first" underlined
remove the bold
To change the note number (afterwards it will be 2.0):
change version 1.0 to 2.0

Pending
Pending items are the work still to do, kept apart from the note history. Each project has its list right above the notes.

Add and order
Type in “Add a pending item…” and press Add (or Enter): the new item goes to the end of the open ones. Open items are numbered from 1; completed ones go to the end, struck through and without a number. Move item up and Move item down (the arrows on each row) move an item one place.

Complete, edit and remove
The checkbox completes the item and moves it to the end; if you uncheck it, it returns to the end of the open ones. Edit pending item (the pencil) changes the text in place: Enter or leaving the field saves, Esc cancels and an empty text keeps the old one. Remove pending item (the ×) deletes it at once, with no confirmation and no notice with Undo.

In the AI panel
The Pending row of the AI panel has four buttons. Extract asks the model to read the history and add what is missing: it needs a connected model and those items carry the AI tag. Add leaves the phrase “Add a pending item:” in the chat box to complete; without a model, use the first request of the practice. Confirm and Remove need no model: they list the open items with their number in the chat; tick the ones you want and press Apply. With a model connected, the assistant also manages pending items (chapter 3.2).

Practice · without AI
In Practice, start with no open items (completed ones are not numbered, so they do not get in the way). The text goes in double quotes; without them the request does not run locally.
add the task "Write note 1.0"
add the task "Try the formatting"
To add one at the very top:
add the task at the top "Read the help"
To see the numbered list in the chat:
show the pending tasks
Each number is the one the item has at that moment: moving one changes the others. To reorder, give the target position: one to first place, another a place up and another a place down:
move pending 3 to first place
move pending 3 to position 2
move pending 1 to position 2
To complete one item, change the text of another and remove another:
mark pending 2 as done
edit pending 2 "Read the help and this guide"
remove pending 1

Save and backups
Your work lives in this browser and is protected on three levels: autosave, the Save button and the Backup button, the only one that survives clearing the browser or changing computers.

Autosave
Every change is saved by itself a moment later. The line under the footer buttons says “saving…” while it waits, “unsaved” if autosave is off and, when done, the time of the last save. In Settings, Autosave turns it on or off and Save interval picks 250 ms, 500 ms, 1 s or 2 s. Save settings closes the panel and saves any settings still pending.

Save
Save saves the changes of every project at once, even with autosave off. A notice says “Saved.” Shortcut: Ctrl/Cmd+S.

Backup
Backup downloads a JSON with the whole database, without your API keys. It is the real save: make one before clearing the browser or changing computers. Backups can also be encrypted (chapter 2.2).

Import
Import takes two kinds of file. A backup JSON restores the logbook: it replaces every project with the file’s, keeps the API keys already saved and confirms with “Database imported.” and an Undo button for a few seconds. A TXT, Markdown, DOCX or PDF file creates a new project named after the file, with its text in note 1.0. DOCX and PDF need a connection: they load an external reader.

Memory only
If the browser blocks local storage, the “Memory only” notice appears: changes last only in that tab and are lost on reload. Make a backup then.

Practice · without AI
Press Backup to download a backup. These requests run locally:
save
import a backup
The second leaves a card in the chat with Choose file…, because the browser requires you to pick the file yourself. Pick the backup you just downloaded: projects, notes and pending items stay the same, but the chat goes back to the moment of the backup (the two requests of this practice disappear) and the first project of the file opens, this guide, even if you were in another one. You can also ask for the backup in the chat:
make a backup

Export
Export creates a file to read, print or share, in TXT, DOCX or PDF. It is not a backup: the JSON only comes out through Backup (chapter 2.0).

What each button exports
Export offers the three formats and is in three places: the one in the footer of the sidebar exports all projects, the one in a project header exports that project and the one in a note exports only that note. Pending items, chat and analyses are not exported.

File name
Of the project name, letters, numbers, _ and - are kept; anything else becomes _, and several in a row merge into one. A project called “My project: v1.0 / test” gives My_project_v1_0_test.txt. A note adds -v and its number at the end: note 1.0 ends in -v1_0.txt. All projects come out as bitacora-todo-YYYY-MM-DD (the date is UTC).

What each format contains
TXT is plain text: the project carries its name and description and, for each note, “VERSION n” and its text; a note exported alone, only “VERSION n” and its text. DOCX and PDF keep font, size, bold, italic, underline and strikethrough, and when you export a single note they add the project name.

Online and offline
DOCX is created in the browser itself and works offline. PDF loads a library (jsPDF) from the internet: offline it shows a notice and downloads nothing. The PDF also draws well only Latin letters with accents, ñ, the quotation marks «» and the euro sign; ▲ ▼ ✓ →, emojis, Cyrillic and Chinese, Japanese or Korean come out garbled (note 1.2 uses ▲ ▼). If your text has them, export to DOCX.

Practice · without AI
The requests export with no model. For the practice project:
export the project Practice as txt
export the project Practice as docx
export the project Practice as pdf
For all projects:
export everything as txt
export all projects as docx
Without a model, a note is exported only with its Export button: there is no local request for it.

Encryption and APIs copy
Two files can carry secrets: the Backup, with your logbook, and the APIs copy, with your AI providers and their keys. Both can be protected with a password. None of this needs a model.

Two different copies
The Backup never carries your API keys. The keys go apart: in Settings, Export APIs saves the URLs, models and keys of your providers and Import APIs restores them. When you import, the file overwrites the providers it lists and the active provider; an empty key never erases a saved one. Without encryption, the file holds your keys in plain text: treat it like a password.

Encrypt with a password
Two checkboxes in Settings protect the files. The password has at least 8 characters and the encryption is AES-256-GCM, with the key derived from it (PBKDF2-SHA-256, 600,000 iterations).
“Encrypt the file with a password” protects the APIs file: every export asks for a password, with confirmation, and it is not stored anywhere.
“Encrypt the backup with a password” protects the backup: the password is stored in this browser, like the API keys, and backups come out encrypted without asking. Change password renews it and unchecking the box deletes it.

Open an encrypted file
When you import, the program detects that the file is encrypted and asks for the password. With a wrong password nothing is imported. When you open an encrypted backup, its password is saved automatically (if it has 8 characters or more) and the next backups are encrypted with it. Without the password there is no way to open the file: write it down somewhere safe. If the browser does not offer Web Crypto, encryption is not available and nothing is ever written in the clear.

With the assistant
The password is always typed in the program’s dialog, not in the chat. If you type one there in quotes, after an equals sign or with the look of a key, it is replaced by •••••• before the message is saved or sent; a one-word password without quotes is not detected, so do not type it in the chat. The assistant needs neither your API keys nor your passwords, and it does not read them.

Practice · without AI
No real key is needed: with your providers as they are, everything works the same. In Settings, check “Encrypt the file with a password”, press Export APIs, type a password of 8 characters or more and repeat it. A file downloads that can no longer be read in a text editor. Then press Import APIs, pick that file and type the password: it restores the same thing you just exported, so nothing changes.
The equivalent request asks the program for the export, which opens the password dialog:
export the APIs encrypted
For the backup: check “Encrypt the backup with a password”, type a password in Settings and press Backup. The file comes out encrypted, without asking. Uncheck the box when you finish: it deletes the saved password.

Connect a model
The AI assistant is optional. Without a model, the history, the editors, search, reversions and projects work the same. With a model, the assistant reads the project history and answers, summarizes, analyzes changes and rewrites.

Choose a provider
In Settings, “Active provider” comes first. You can choose LM Studio, Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, xAI/Grok, Groq, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Mistral AI or Together AI. When you choose one, its configuration appears right below: base URL, model and API key, with Detect models to list the ones it offers. Each provider comes with a suggested URL and model; change them if your server uses others. Keys are saved in this browser’s profile. “No AI” removes the provider.

Local or cloud
LM Studio and Ollama run on your computer and usually only need CORS enabled on the local server. Cloud providers receive the requests straight from the browser, with your key, and may depend on CORS and on the provider’s policies: check their terms before sending sensitive information. Anthropic accepts direct calls from the browser only with its direct-access mode that supports CORS, which the program already turns on in every request. For a fully local workflow, use LM Studio or Ollama.

The model chip
Next to the AI button there is a chip with the status: “No AI” with no provider (press it and it opens Settings), an amber dot if a cloud provider is missing its key and a green dot when it is ready. With a model connected it shows provider and model; press it to filter and switch models, use Detect models or go to Settings.

Model profile
Small models (up to about 5B parameters) get lost with long requests. The Model profile, in Settings, solves that. Automatic decides by the size in the model name: 5B or less, compact; no recognizable size, full. Compact and Full set it by hand. In compact the assistant sends short, single-task requests: the program picks the context, decides the action and reads the answer, and the model only writes.

What changes without a model
Everything that does not need writing keeps working: notes, pending items, backups, export and the local requests. So does renumbering with quick schemes or with pairs like 1.2 => 2.0 (chapter 3.4) and opening an analysis already saved (chapter 3.3). Without a model, the AI panel says so and changes nothing. What needs a model: answering questions, summarizing, extracting pending items, analyzing new changes and rewriting.

Practice · without AI
Open the AI panel and press Extract. The chat says there is no provider and the pending items stay as they were.

Practice · with AI
You need a model, local or in the cloud. With Ollama, for example: in Settings, choose Ollama in “Active provider”, press Detect models and pick one. Open the AI panel: the chip shows the green dot and the model name. Type in the panel box and press Send; if an answer arrives, the model is connected:
Hi, are you connected? Answer in one sentence.
To check that it reads the history of this guide, open it and ask (the answer is “Encryption and APIs copy”):
What is the title of note 2.2?

Quick actions and questions
The AI panel offers two ways to ask: buttons with a ready-written request and a chat box to ask anything. In both, the assistant works with the history of the open project; the project line in the panel says which one it is and how many versions it has. The conversation is saved with the project and travels in the backup. This whole chapter needs a connected model (chapter 3.0).

Quick actions
Summary tells the state of the project: objective, latest version and visible risks. Changes compares the three most recent versions and says which version introduces each change. Contradictions looks for incompatible instructions, contradictory decisions and possible reversions. Extract reads the history and adds to Pending what is missing (chapter 1.3). Each button writes its request in the chat, sends it and leaves the answer below. Renumber versions, next to Summary, is something else (chapter 3.4).

Questions
Type in the box and press Send. Ask why a decision was made, what changed between two versions or what is still pending. The assistant tells what is recorded apart from what it infers, invents nothing that is not in the history and always answers in the language of the interface, even if the notes are in another. If you ask for code that is not already in a version, it explains that its job is to consult and organize the project’s history, not to generate new code.

Long histories
If the history does not fit in a single request, it is sent in consecutive batches, cut between versions. Each result appears in the chat as it finishes (Batch 1 of 3 · 1.0 → 1.26), each batch receives the findings of the previous one and only the final answer updates the pending items. If a batch fails, the earlier ones are kept and the error says which one it was.

Ask how the program is used
When you ask about use (where a button is, what it does, which steps to follow), the program adds its own Help to the request and the assistant answers with it. It does not do this with requests to act or with the quick-action buttons.

Pending items from the chat
Add leaves “Add a pending item:” in the box. Complete the phrase and send it: the model writes the task into Pending, with the AI tag, and confirms it in the chat. Confirm and Remove list the open pending items so you can tick the ones you want (chapter 1.3).

Practice · with AI
Questions about this guide can be asked in the guide itself: they only add messages to the chat of your copy.
What is the difference between Save and Backup?
What does the guide say about exporting to PDF?
Where is the button to export a note?
The third is a question about use: the program adds the Help to it. For the buttons, go to “Practice” and press Summary, Changes and Contradictions; with few notes the answers will be short. Finally, write down a pending item from the chat:
Add a pending item: Reread note 1.0 of Practice

The assistant runs the program
Everything the interface does can be asked of the assistant, and it runs it instead of explaining it. Each action leaves a terminal-style card in the chat: the request, shaped like $ name --key value, and below it ✓ with the result or ✗ with the error. The note or list it touches stays in view.

What it can do
Projects: create, rename, change the description, select, search, export and delete. Notes: create, write, duplicate, select, search, copy, change their number, mark that they revert another and format (font, size, bold, italic, underline and strikethrough, on the whole note or on a fragment); also analyze changes (chapter 3.3) and renumber (chapter 3.4). Pending items: list, add, edit, complete or reopen, move and remove. Copies: save, backup, import, export the APIs, encryption and memory. Settings: language, zoom, autosave, model profile and provider. And undo, open Help and open Settings.

Local requests and requests to the model
Clear one-line requests run locally, without calling the model: they work with no provider and they are the ones in the “without AI” practices. Any other sentence is interpreted by the model, which decides the action: also when the format is missing, when the target is ambiguous (a fragment without quotes, a note without a number) or when what you type is a question. With no model, those sentences only get the notice that there is no provider.

Permissions
Almost everything runs as soon as you ask: your request is the permission. There are two exceptions. Import needs you to pick the file, because the browser requires it: the card carries Choose file…. And whatever could make you lose something asks for confirmation, with Confirm and Cancel on the card: deleting a project or a note, replacing the text of a note, removing the AI, renumbering, deleting all analyses, exporting the APIs in plain text and turning off an encryption. If a dialog is open, close it before sending a request: the chat does not accept it.

What it does not do
It does not read your API keys or your passwords (chapter 2.2), and the result of an action does not go back to the model. By design there is no action for the project icon (it needs an image) or for rewriting a selection (it is a gesture on the chosen text and it calls the AI: chapter 3.4).

Undo
The undo request reverts the last thing that can be undone, such as renumbering or deleting a note: once, and for 10 minutes (chapter 1.1).

Assistant memory
Memory is the assistant’s chat, of one project or of all. In the header of the AI panel, Import memory and Export memory sit to the left of Clear chat and Close AI panel. Each button asks for the scope: This project or All projects. Export downloads a JSON with only the id, the name and the chat of each project, with no notes or keys; if every chat is empty, it says so and downloads nothing. Import pairs each project by id and, failing that, by name, and never creates projects; if the destination chat already has messages, it asks Replace or Add. Import and Clear chat offer Undo.

Practice · without AI
Paste these requests into the chat of “Practice”. Each one leaves its card:
export the memory
change the language to Spanish
change the language to English
The second and the third change the language of the interface and put it back; it can also be changed with the selector in the top bar.

Practice · with AI
With a model connected, ask in your own words. If you do not have those notes, use the numbers you have:
Create a new note in Practice with the text "Testing the assistant"
Duplicate note 1.1
Mark note 1.2 as a reversion of 1.1
Change the project description: say it is my practice project
Delete note 1.2
The last one asks for confirmation: press Cancel and nothing is deleted.

Analyze changes
Analyze changes compares a note with the previous one in the history and explains what changed and why it matters. It is not a text diff: it is a semantic explanation. Generating a new analysis needs a connected model (chapter 3.0); opening a saved one does not.

What it returns
The analysis header shows the pair of versions, for example 1.2.0 → 1.3.0. It always opens with a status: CHANGES DETECTED, NO CHANGES, NO RELATION (the notes cover different matters) or INCONCLUSIVE RESULT (what is written does not allow telling). Then come the summary, the relevant changes, the impact or risks and a conclusion.

Generate, save and repeat
Analyze changes is at the top of each note (chapter 1.2). The analysis opens in a block on the note and can be saved as a comment of the version. Reanalyze asks for a new one. If you save several analyses of the same note, Previous and Latest step through them. A note with a saved analysis shows, next to HISTORY, a pill with the ≠ symbol and the word ANALYSIS, with ×n when there are several: it opens and closes the analysis with no model.

When it disappears
Editing the text of a note deletes its saved analysis, so that none stays out of date without warning. You can also delete them from the assistant.

Without a model and with small models
Without a model you can open saved analyses, with Analyze changes or with the pill. Generating a new one needs a provider; without it, the program says so and does not pass off a shallow diff as an analysis. With the compact profile (chapter 3.0), only the removed and added sentences are sent, and two identical notes do not call the model.

With the assistant
You can ask it to analyze a note, to analyze it again, to show an analysis (the latest, the previous one, one by its order number or one containing some text) or to delete it: one or all. These requests are recognized locally, without the model deciding the action: showing and deleting need no model; analyzing and analyzing again do, because the model writes the analysis, saves the result in the note, opens its block and summarizes it in the chat. Deleting all asks for confirmation (chapter 3.2).

Practice · without AI
The demos come with saved analyses and you need no model to read them. Go to the thesis project and bring note 0.5 into view; its status is CHANGES DETECTED:
select the project Thesis
select the note 0.5
Press the pill with ≠ and ANALYSIS next to HISTORY: the analysis opens and another click closes it. Note 0.8 is a case of NO RELATION. The EP project shows the other two statuses: the note called Master (INCONCLUSIVE RESULT) and the note called Release (NO CHANGES). To see several analyses of a single note, open Lumen Commerce, note 1.4.0, which carries ×3:
select the project Lumen
select the note 1.4.0
Open it and step through with Previous and Latest.

Practice · with AI
You need a model (chapter 3.0). In “Practice”, write a different text in each of notes 1.1 and 1.2 (if you do not have them, use two in a row) and ask in your own words. Each request leaves its card and the note stays in view; the status and the text of the analysis depend on your model:
Analyze the changes of note 1.2
Reanalyze note 1.2
Show the previous analysis of note 1.2
Delete the analysis of note 1.2
Deleting all asks for confirmation: press Cancel and nothing is deleted.
Delete all the analyses

Rewrite and renumber versions
Two tools that change the text or the numbering, and neither touches anything until you confirm.

Rewrite a fragment
Select a piece of a note: the selection panel appears, with the REWRITE label. Choose a style: Professional, Reflective, Technical, Concise or Suggestion. The request and the proposal stay in the chat and the note does not change until you press Apply. Before that you can copy the proposal, discard it or refine it with another instruction, for example “Shorter, and drop the date.”. Rewriting needs a model and has no chat request: it is a gesture on the chosen text (chapter 3.2).

Renumber versions
Renumber versions, in the AI panel next to Summary, asks the assistant to review the numbering of the project and propose another that fits its pace. The proposal appears in the chat with the current and the new number of each version, and nothing changes until you press Accept. Accepting renames every version and keeps the Reverts relations; Undo brings the previous numbering back. If you edit versions by hand before accepting, the proposal expires. If the current numbering already fits, the chat says so, there is nothing to apply and it offers Another scheme and four quick schemes. Another scheme lets you ask for a different numbering by typing the one you prefer in the chat box (semantic, integers only or year.month): the model answers.

Renumber without a model
Some ways are computed locally: the four quick schemes the chat offers (1.0.0, integers only, year.month and major.minor) and written pairs. They do not call the AI, work with no provider and give the same notice, with Accept and Undo. Year.month uses the date of each note; semantic and major.minor only raise the minor number, one at a time. To decide which version opens a milestone, type pairs in the chat, by number, by name or by position with #: 1.2 => 2.0; #3 -> 3.1. A question like “If I do 1.2 -> 2.0, what changes?” is not a pair and goes to the AI. If the plan is impossible (a repeated number or a version with two numbers), the chat gives the reason and does not call the AI either.

Practice · without AI
In “Practice”, paste this pair into the assistant chat (if you do not have notes 1.1 and 1.2, use the numbers you have):
1.1 => 3.0; 1.2 -> 3.1
The chat proposes the renumbering and changes nothing. Press Accept: the notes become 3.0 and 3.1. To put them back, press Undo.

Practice · with AI
You need a model (chapter 3.0). To rewrite, write in a note of “Practice” the sentence “Today I tried the formatting and the requests of the guide and almost everything worked the first time”, select it and choose Concise. Read the proposal in the chat and press Apply, or discard it.
To renumber, press Renumber versions. If you do not like the proposal, or if the chat says the numbering already fits, press Another scheme and type in the chat box:
integers only
The model answers with another proposal. Press Accept and then Undo to get the numbers back. Finally, a question, which also goes to the model:
If I do 1.1 -> 3.0, what changes?

pending.text: Create a practice project called “Practice”.
In “Practice”, add a note with “New version note” and duplicate it.
In note 1.0 of “Practice”, write a sentence and format it: bold and size 16, italic, one fragment underlined and remove the bold.
In “Practice”, add a pending item with “Add”, change its text with the pencil and complete it with its checkbox.
In “Practice”, with requests: add three pending items, show them, reorder them, complete one, edit another and remove another.
Save with “Save”, download a “Backup” and restore it with “Import”.
Export “Practice” as TXT and as DOCX, with the button or with a request, and export one note with the note’s button.
Encrypt the APIs with “Encrypt the file with a password”, export them, import them with their password and make an encrypted backup.
Choose a provider in “Active provider”, detect its models, check the chip next to the AI button and send the assistant a greeting.
With a model: ask something about this guide, press “Summary” in “Practice” and write down a pending item by typing “Add a pending item: …” in the chat.
Give the assistant requests: export the memory and change the language without a model; with a model, create and duplicate a note, mark a reversion and cancel a deletion.
Open a saved analysis of the demo with the ≠ ANALYSIS pill and, with a model, analyze the changes of a note in “Practice”.
Rewrite a fragment of “Practice” with a style and apply it, and renumber its notes with a written pair: accept it and undo it.
Open this guide and read note 1.0.

projects.name: Thesis · Blue Carbon in Salt Marshes
projects.description: Doctoral thesis on how much carbon the salt marshes of an Atlantic estuary accumulate and how much methane they emit, using soil cores, dating and gas chambers.

versions.instructions:
Central question: do the estuary’s salt marshes store more carbon than they emit (CO₂ and CH₄ combined)?
Working hypothesis: above a salinity of 18, methane stays limited and the net balance is negative, meaning a sink.
Planned structure: 6 chapters (introduction, methods, carbon accumulation, gas fluxes, balance and discussion, conclusions). First full draft to the supervisor on June 30.

projects.name: Atlas API Gateway
projects.description: Gateway shared by internal services for routing, authentication, traffic limits and traceability.

versions.instructions:
Scope agreed with Payments, Users and Orders: the gateway routes, authenticates and rate-limits traffic, but does not transform request bodies.

Decisions:
- Envoy as the data plane and our own control plane in Go, so we do not depend on a third party’s dynamic configuration API.
- Authentication is delegated to Cinder Auth Vault; the gateway only validates tokens and forwards the identity in a signed internal header.
- A single error format for every service (code, message and correlation-id), so clients do not have to interpret different responses.

Out of scope for v1: federated GraphQL and WebSockets.
Main risk: the control plane becoming a single point of failure. Planned mitigation: replicas that cache the last valid configuration locally.

Declarative YAML routes with schema validation on load (atlas lint). Every request gets an x-correlation-id that travels to all services; if a valid one already arrives, it is kept.
First routes migrated: /users, /orders and /health.

Atomic configuration: the control plane validates the whole set and only then publishes it under a version number. If validation fails, the gateway keeps the last good configuration and raises an alert.
No more half-applied reloads, the state that caused the February 3 outage.

Per-client, per-endpoint limit with a fixed window in Redis. First load test: p95 of 18 ms at 4,000 rps.
Problem: legitimate traffic is rejected at the start of every minute (window-boundary effect).

The fixed window is replaced by a token bucket (atomic Lua script in Redis). It allows bursts of up to 5× the sustained rate; 429s at peak drop from 0.3% to 0.02%.
